title: Tightest Group of K Scores
statement:
You get a list of student scores and a number k. Choose any k students. The spread of a group is its highest score minus its lowest score.

Return the smallest spread any group of exactly k students can have. The chosen students do not need to be next to each other in the list.

examples.why: Sorted: 12 15 37 40 90. The groups of three neighbours spread 25, 25 and 53. Students far apart in the input (12 and 15) end up next to each other.
A single student has the same highest and lowest score.
The two 9s form a group with no spread at all.

hints: Suppose the scores were sorted. Which k scores could possibly form the tightest group?
In sorted order, the best group is always k consecutive scores: replacing any outer member with one in between can only shrink the spread.
Sort, then slide a window of length k and take the smallest scores[i + k − 1] − scores[i].

explain.intuition:
Only the lowest and highest members of a group affect its spread. Once the scores are sorted, take any group and look at its lowest and highest member. Every score lying between them could join the group for free, so the best group with that lowest member is simply the next k − 1 scores after it.

That turns the search over all groups into a window of fixed size sliding over the sorted list. The spread of the window starting at i is sorted[i + k − 1] − sorted[i].
steps: Sort a copy of scores in ascending order.
For every i from 0 to n − k, compute sorted[i + k − 1] − sorted[i].
Return the smallest of those values.
pitfalls: Sliding a window over the unsorted list, which only looks at students who happen to be next to each other.
Using sorted[i + k] − sorted[i]: a window of k elements ends at index i + k − 1.
Sorting numbers in JavaScript without a comparator, which sorts them as strings (100 before 20).

solutions.title: Best group for each lowest member
solutions.idea: For every student as the lowest score, collect all scores at least that large, sort them, and take the k-th smallest.

solutions.title: Sort and slide a window of k
solutions.idea: In sorted order the tightest group is k consecutive scores, so check every window.
